mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of episodes where INDPRO declines for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 over the prior six months indicates robust residential investment, which boosts construction and related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, GDPC1) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods where HOUST and GDPC1 are strongly positively correlated over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k per month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate higher earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS exceeds 250,000 for three straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average for more than one year indicates heightened consumer spending financed by debt, which supports near-term corporate revenues but increases vulnerability to a correction; this mechanism predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days unless a debt distress signal appears.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS remains below its 5-year average for over a year.
